grow/problem: The power rule finds the slope of x cubed at every x, with no measuring. There, x is the base: the number being multiplied. In e to the x, x has moved up into the power, so the power rule does not apply.
grow/bank: Go back to the bank that grows a dollar by a hundred percent a year, at every instant. At each moment, it adds interest at a hundred percent of whatever is there now.
grow/rate: So the money grows at a rate equal to the amount. Two dollars grow at two dollars a year, and five dollars at five.
grow/slide: On the curve of e to the x, the rate is the slope, and the amount is the height. Slide the tangent along it: at every point, the slope equals the height.
grow/one: The tangent always meets the axis one step to the left, so its rise over that run of one is the height itself. At x equals one, both are two point seven two.
grow/rule: So e to the x is its own derivative: e to the x becomes e to the x.
fast/three: Now put a three in the power: e to the three x. At x equals one, its power is already three, so it gets to each height in a third of the time.
fast/squeeze: Its curve is the curve of e to the x, squeezed sideways to a third of its width.
fast/steep: Squeezing keeps every rise but cuts every run to a third, so each slope is three times as steep: three times the height.
fast/zero: Check it at zero. There the power is zero, and e to the zero is one: the height is one, and the measured slope is three.
fast/rule: So the three comes out in front: e to the three x becomes three e to the three x. For any number a, e to the a x becomes a times e to the a x.
mirror/ln: Now ln x. It reads e to the x backwards: give it a height, and it returns the x. So its curve is the same curve with the two axes swapped: mirrored across the diagonal.
mirror/point: e to the x reaches height two at about zero point six nine. In the mirror, that point lands at x equals two, with height zero point six nine: ln two.
mirror/swap: The tangent is mirrored too. There it rose two for every one across. In the mirror, rise and run trade places: one up for every two across, a slope of a half.
mirror/every: Any point works the same way. Where e to the x has height five, its slope is five, so ln, at five, has slope one fifth.
mirror/rule: The slope of ln at any x is one over x: ln x becomes one over x.
try/p1: Now mix all three kinds: a power, an exponential, and a log. A sum is differentiated one piece at a time.
try/t1: Two x cubed is a power: the three comes down, and three times two is six. Six x squared.
try/t2: Four e to the minus two x: the minus two comes out in front. Four times minus two is minus eight, so minus eight e to the minus two x.
try/t3: Three ln x becomes three over x. It is subtracted, so its derivative is subtracted as well: minus three over x.
try/sum: Put the three pieces back together, signs and all, and that is f prime of x.
try/p2: For the slope at one point, differentiate first. x squared plus six ln x becomes two x, plus six over x.
try/a2: Then put in two. Two x is four, and six over x is three, so f prime of two is seven.
try/zero: For five e to the three x, the three comes out: fifteen e to the three x. At zero, e to the zero is one, so the slope there is fifteen, not the height, five.
